title: Your first scene
cards/0/body: Create a scene, a camera and a renderer, make a cube, put it in the scene and ask the renderer to draw.
cards/1/task: The screen is empty. Turn on lines of code until the cube shows up. Above is real Three.js.
cards/2/q: Why is the cube invisible when camera.position.z = 0?
cards/2/options/0: The camera is inside the cube: from inside, the faces point away from us and are not drawn
cards/2/explain: Both the camera and the cube start at (0, 0, 0). That is why you move the camera back.
cards/3/body: By default the camera sits at the origin and looks down the −Z axis, "into the screen". So you move it back along +Z: camera.position.z = 5. Y points up, X points right.
cards/4/items/1: Create the camera and move it back
cards/4/items/2: Create the renderer and add its canvas to the page
cards/4/items/3: Create a Mesh and add it to the scene
cards/4/explain: The creation order matters less than calling render once everything is ready.
cards/5/q: Which line keeps the cube from showing up?
cards/5/explain: The cube is created but never added to the scene: scene.add(cube) is missing. The renderer only draws the scene.
cards/6/q: A Mesh from a geometry and a material
cards/6/explain: Three.js has no Cube class. A cube is a Mesh with a BoxGeometry.
cards/7/pairs/1/1: Colors by face direction, needs no light
cards/7/pairs/2/1: The canvas element for the page
cards/7/pairs/3/1: Put an object into the world
cards/8/q: Where does a Three.js camera look by default?
cards/8/explain: To look at a specific point, use camera.lookAt(x, y, z).
